audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer uses TWO fabricated ability names — 'Golden Onslaught' and 'Final Retribution' — neither of which is Zaahen's. It uses them in whys[1], whys[3], spikes[2], early, late and wants.foe[1]. The full layer is worse: it never names a single ability, calling his R literally 'Ultimate' in fourteen places including focus.text.
audit.why: The brief's missingInteractions payload names his real kit: The Darkin Glaive (Q), Dreaded Return (W), Aureate Rush (E), Grim Deliverance (R). 'Golden Onslaught' is used for the thing that walks you down at level 2, which is the E dash — Aureate Rush. 'Final Retribution' is used for the single-target ult — Grim Deliverance. This is the same class of error as 'Ares of Blaze' for Pyroclasm. Worse, whys[3] attributes a 'reset' to the ultimate; the kit puts the auto-attack reset on Q (The Darkin Glaive), not R, so both the name AND the mechanic were wrong in one sentence.
audit.corrected: All six fabricated-name occurrences replaced with the real names, and the reset re-attributed from R to Q where the kit actually places it.
sources: missingInteractions headlines naming The Darkin Glaive (Q), Dreaded Return (W), Aureate Rush (E), Grim Deliverance (R)

audit.whatIsWrong: Content win[1] says Gnar and win[3] says Skill, while whys[1] opens 'Level 2 is Zaahen's' and whys[3] opens 'Levels 4-5 are his again'. The full layer has the same two stages wrong.
audit.why: The enum directly contradicts the first four words of its own explanation. The packet chart (Skill,Zaahen,Gnar,Zaahen,Skill,Gnar,Gnar) agrees with the prose on every stage.
audit.corrected: Skill / Zaahen / Gnar / Zaahen / Skill / Gnar / Gnar as one atomic group across both layers, with ratings adjusted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer spikes said 'Stridebreaker'; Zaahen's spikes were never dated because no ability was ever named.
audit.why: Grim Deliverance is 110s at rank 1 — his real level-6 threat and a window you can play whole waves around. Aureate Rush at 10s is what makes level 2 his. Dreaded Return at 14s is the cooldown that gates every step-up.
audit.corrected: Phase whys now key to Aureate Rush at level 2 and Grim Deliverance at 4-5 and 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere — needs concrete wait-for-X-before-you-Y lines'. sequencingCues was 0.
audit.why: With no ability names on the full layer there was nothing to sequence around; every cooldown line said 'Ultimate' and 'his big cooldown'.
audit.corrected: Added explicit sequencing: wait for Dreaded Return (14s) to miss before stepping into 850 range; bait Grim Deliverance (110s) before committing Mega; treat The Darkin Glaive's wind-up, not its cast, as the cue to back off.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three flagged interactions never reach the page: Zaahen heals off both The Darkin Glaive and Grim Deliverance, Aureate Rush scales on percent health, and both champions carry displacement.
audit.why: The itemization block recommends Plated Steelcaps and no anti-heal at all, which is the wrong answer twice over — armour does nothing against a percent-health dash, and his Q and R both sustain him through chip. The mutual-displacement point matters because he can recast The Darkin Glaive to knock you up: whoever lands displacement first owns the trade, and Wallop is 7s against his 10s.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal and the percent-health warning added to dontsFull; the displacement race stated in dontsFull[2].d.

notes: Two fabricated ability names found and killed: 'Golden Onslaught' (really Aureate Rush, the E dash) and 'Final Retribution' (really Grim Deliverance, the R), used across six fields. The real names come from the missingInteractions payload, which is the only place in this brief that names Zaahen's kit — packet.enemyAbilities is null and the kit file carries no names. whys[3] compounded the error by attributing a 'reset' to the ultimate; the auto-reset flag is on Q (The Darkin Glaive), so I moved it there and gave R its actual mechanic, the heal. The full layer never named ANY ability, calling his R 'Ultimate' fourteen times, and packet.sequencingCues was 0 — that defect is fixed with concrete waits: Dreaded Return 14s / 850 range, Grim Deliverance 110s, The Darkin Glaive 10s.
unverified: focus.text is the literal string 'Zaahen Ultimate' (15 chars) — under the applier's 25-character skip threshold, so I could not propose replacing it with a real ability name.
